chunks: Muhammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-Yaqṭīnī, who said:

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) sent to me a bundle of clothes, a group of servants, dinars, and funded a pilgrimage for me, a pilgrimage for my brother Musa ibn Ubayd, and a pilgrimage for Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, and ordered us to perform Hajj on his behalf. There was one hundred dinars among us, divided into thirds. When I intended to inspect the clothes, I saw clay in the folds of the garments. I asked the messenger, 'What is this?' He said, 'Whenever goods are sent, clay from the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is placed in them.' Then the messenger said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said, 'It is a guarantee of safety by God's permission.' He ordered matters regarding the money for maintaining his family and needy people, and ordered the payment of three hundred dinars to Ruḥaym, a woman who was his, and ordered me to divorce her on his behalf, and to provide her with maintenance (mut'ah) with this money, and ordered me to witness her divorce before Safwan ibn Yahya and another whom Muhammad ibn ʿĪsā forgot his name.

key_terms.أُمَتِّعَهَا: To provide her with maintenance (mut'ah) upon divorce
key_terms.رُحَيْمَ: Name of the woman being divorced
key_terms.رِزَامَ: A bundle or load of goods
key_terms.مُحَاجِيجَ: Needy people or those in need

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the clay found in the clothes sent by the Imam, and what were the financial instructions regarding Ruḥaym?
ai.summary: Although the summary identifies the sender as Imam al-Rida, the chapter title 'Bab al-Wakala fi al-Talaq' and the specific instruction to divorce Ruḥaym indicate this is a key precedent for proxy divorce (Talaq bi al-Wakala) in Shia jurisprudence. The inclusion of clay from Imam al-Husayn’s grave serves as a spiritual seal of authenticity (Aman), while the financial distribution highlights the Imam’s role in managing communal wealth and personal affairs through trusted agents.
